title: Unit 1 test: Kinematics
author: cm-1
directions: Unit 1 practice test on kinematics, 70 minutes in all. Section I: 12 multiple-choice questions in 25 minutes. Section II: 2 free-response questions in 45 minutes. Any calculator may be used. Take g = 9.8 m/s^2, work in SI units, and say which direction you call positive before you use signs. Total your raw points with the answer key; the total is a practice tally, not an AP® score.

figures.alt: Velocity–time graph made of straight segments: from 2 m/s at t = 0 up to 8 m/s at t = 3 s, constant at 8 m/s until t = 6 s, then down to 0 at t = 8 s.
figures.caption: Velocity of a cart

figures.alt: Blank grid for plotting, 11 squares wide and 7 squares tall, with the horizontal axis labeled t^2 (s^2) and the vertical axis labeled x (m).
Plot of x against t^2 for the six data points from t^2 = 0 to 4.0 s^2, lying close to a straight line through the origin labeled with a slope of about 0.31 m/s^2.

parts.directions: Pick the one best answer to each question. Neglect air resistance.

items.prompt: A displacement vector A has magnitude 12 m and points 150° counterclockwise from the +x-axis. What are its components?
items.rationale: A_x = 12 cos 150° = −10.4 m ≈ −10 m and A_y = 12 sin 150° = +6.0 m. A vector in the second quadrant has a negative x-component and a positive y-component.

distractorNotes.B: Both signs are reversed; this vector points at 330°, in the fourth quadrant.
distractorNotes.C: Sine and cosine are swapped, as if the angle were measured from the y-axis.
distractorNotes.D: Sine and cosine are swapped and both signs are reversed.

items.prompt: Two forces are P = (2.0 i − 5.0 j) N and Q = (−4.0 i + 1.0 j) N. What is the magnitude of P − Q?

distractorNotes.A: This is |P| − |Q| = 5.4 N − 4.1 N; magnitudes do not subtract like that.
distractorNotes.C: This is |P + Q| = |−2.0 i − 4.0 j| = 4.5 N, the sum rather than the difference.
distractorNotes.D: This adds the component sizes 6.0 + 6.0 instead of combining them with the Pythagorean theorem.

items.prompt: A cart's position is x(t) = 3.0t^2 − 0.50t^3, with x in meters and t in seconds. What is the cart's acceleration at t = 3.0 s?

distractorNotes.B: 4.5 is the velocity v(3.0 s) in m/s.
distractorNotes.C: 6.0 m/s^2 is the acceleration at t = 0.
distractorNotes.D: 13.5 is the position x(3.0 s) in meters, not an acceleration.

items.prompt: An object moves along the x-axis with velocity v(t) = 4.0 − 2.0t, in m/s, and is at x = 1.0 m at t = 0. Where is it at t = 3.0 s?

distractorNotes.A: This is the displacement, 3.0 m, without the starting position.
distractorNotes.B: This adds the distance traveled (4.0 m out, then 1.0 m back) to the start instead of the displacement.
distractorNotes.C: −2.0 m/s is the velocity at 3.0 s, not a position.

items.prompt: A cart starts from rest at the origin with acceleration a(t) = 2.0t, in m/s^2. How far has it traveled at t = 3.0 s?
items.rationale: v = 1.0t^2 (from rest) and x = t^3/3, so x(3.0 s) = 27/3 = 9.0 m.

distractorNotes.B: This uses the average acceleration, 3.0 m/s^2, in ½at^2, which is valid only for constant acceleration.
distractorNotes.C: This uses the final acceleration, 6.0 m/s^2, in ½at^2.
distractorNotes.D: This multiplies 2.0 by t^2 without integrating.

items.prompt: The graph shows the velocity of a cart along a straight track. What is the cart's displacement from t = 0 to t = 8.0 s?
items.rationale: Displacement is the area under the graph: a trapezoid from 0 to 3.0 s, ½(2.0 + 8.0)(3.0) = 15 m; a rectangle from 3.0 to 6.0 s, 24 m; a triangle from 6.0 to 8.0 s, 8.0 m. Total 47 m.

distractorNotes.A: This treats the first 3.0 s as a triangle starting from zero velocity, missing the initial 2.0 m/s.
distractorNotes.C: This multiplies the largest velocity by the whole time.
distractorNotes.D: 8.0 m/s is the largest velocity, not a displacement.

items.prompt: For the cart whose velocity graph is shown, at which time is the magnitude of its acceleration greatest?
choices: The magnitude is the same at all three times.
items.rationale: Acceleration is the slope: 2.0 m/s^2 from 0 to 3.0 s, zero from 3.0 to 6.0 s, and −4.0 m/s^2 from 6.0 to 8.0 s, so its magnitude is greatest at 7.0 s.

distractorNotes.A: The slope there is 2.0 m/s^2, half the magnitude at 7.0 s.
distractorNotes.B: The graph is flat there, so the acceleration is zero even though the velocity is largest.
distractorNotes.D: The slopes differ on the three intervals.

items.prompt:
A motion sensor gives a cart's position:
| t (s) | 0 | 1.0 | 2.0 | 3.0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| x (m) | 0 | 0.80 | 3.20 | 7.20 |
Which description fits the data?
choices: Constant acceleration of 1.6 m/s^2, starting from rest
Constant acceleration of 0.80 m/s^2, starting from rest
An acceleration that increases with time
items.rationale: x is proportional to t^2 (0.80, 3.20 and 7.20 are 0.80 × 1, 4 and 9), so x = ½at^2 with ½a = 0.80 m/s^2 and a = 1.6 m/s^2, starting from rest.

distractorNotes.A: 2.4 m/s is the average velocity over 3.0 s; the position does not change by equal amounts each second.
distractorNotes.C: This takes the coefficient 0.80 m/s^2 as the acceleration and forgets the factor ½.
distractorNotes.D: The second differences are constant (1.6 m each), so the acceleration is constant.

items.prompt: A boat that moves at 5.0 m/s relative to the water heads straight across a 60 m wide river that flows at 3.0 m/s. How far downstream of its starting point does it land?
items.rationale: Crossing time = 60 m/5.0 m/s = 12 s; in that time the current carries the boat 3.0 m/s × 12 s = 36 m downstream.

distractorNotes.A: This divides the width by the current speed, which is not a time the boat spends doing anything.
distractorNotes.B: This uses the ratio 3.0/4.0 from a 3-4-5 triangle with the wrong side.
distractorNotes.C: This assumes the drift equals the river's width.

items.prompt: A helicopter flies east at 40 m/s relative to the ground while a balloon drifts south at 9.0 m/s. What is the balloon's velocity relative to the helicopter?
items.rationale: v_BH = v_BG − v_HG = (0 i − 9.0 j) − (40 i) = −40 i − 9.0 j m/s, which is √(40^2 + 9.0^2) = 41 m/s at arctan(9.0/40) = 13° south of west.

distractorNotes.B: This is the helicopter's velocity relative to the balloon, v_HB, which has the opposite direction.
distractorNotes.C: This adds the speeds and ignores that the velocities are perpendicular.
distractorNotes.D: This subtracts the speeds, 40 − 9.0, instead of subtracting vectors.

items.prompt: A particle's position is r(t) = (3.0t^2) i + (4.0t) j, with r in meters and t in seconds. What is its speed at t = 2.0 s?
items.rationale: v = dr/dt = 6.0t i + 4.0 j, so v(2.0 s) = 12 i + 4.0 j m/s and the speed is √(12^2 + 4.0^2) = 12.6 m/s ≈ 13 m/s.

distractorNotes.A: 6.0 m/s^2 is the magnitude of the acceleration.
distractorNotes.B: This is the distance from the origin, |r(2.0 s)| = |12 i + 8.0 j| = 14 m.

items.prompt: Ball A rolls off the edge of a 1.8 m high table at 3.0 m/s. At the same instant, ball B is dropped from rest from the same height beside the table. Neglect air resistance. Which statement is correct?
choices: They land at the same time, with ball A about 1.8 m from the foot of the table.
They land at the same time, with ball A about 3.0 m from the foot of the table.
items.rationale: Both start with zero vertical velocity, so both fall 1.8 m in t = √(2(1.8)/9.8) = 0.61 s. Ball A moves 3.0 m/s × 0.61 s = 1.8 m horizontally.

distractorNotes.A: The horizontal motion does not slow the vertical fall.
distractorNotes.B: The horizontal motion does not speed up the vertical fall either.
distractorNotes.D: This assumes a flight time of 1.0 s.

parts.directions: Show your reasoning, with units, in every part. Allow about 20 minutes for Question 1 (10 points) and 25 minutes for Question 2 (10 points). Question 2 is a paper investigation with supplied, invented data; such investigations do not replace the hands-on laboratory work the course framework calls for, and they do not count toward the AP Course Audit or college lab credit.

items.prompt: A small rover drives on a level test field. With x pointing east and y pointing north, its position is r(t) = (0.50t^2 − 2.0t) i + (6.0t − 0.75t^2) j, with r in meters and t in seconds, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 6.0 s.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the rover's velocity v(t) and acceleration a(t) as vectors.

rubric.criterion: Differentiates the x-component: v_x = 1.0t − 2.0 (m/s).
Differentiates the y-component: v_y = 6.0 − 1.5t (m/s).
Gives a = (1.0 i − 1.5 j) m/s^2, constant, with units.

steps: Differentiate each component of r with the power rule.
Differentiate each component of v; both are constants.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the time at which the rover is moving due north, and its speed at that time.

rubric.criterion: Sets v_x = 0 with v_y > 0 and finds t = 2.0 s.
Speed 3.0 m/s (accept 2.9–3.1 m/s).

steps: Due north means v_x = 0 and v_y > 0: 1.0t − 2.0 = 0 gives t = 2.0 s.
v_y(2.0) = 6.0 − 3.0 = 3.0 m/s, so the speed is 3.0 m/s.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the rover's displacement from t = 0 to t = 6.0 s, both as a vector and as a magnitude.

rubric.criterion: Magnitude 10.8 m (accept 10.7–10.9 m, or 11 m).

parts.answer: Δr = (6.0 i + 9.0 j) m, magnitude 10.8 m.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Is the rover speeding up, slowing down, or neither at t = 1.0 s? Justify your answer using the velocity and acceleration vectors.

rubric.criterion: Evaluates v(1.0 s) = (−1.0 i + 4.5 j) m/s.
Shows that the component of a along v is negative, for example a · v = (1.0)(−1.0) + (−1.5)(4.5) = −7.75 m^2/s^3 < 0.
Concludes that the rover is slowing down, consistent with the sign found.

parts.answer: Slowing down: v(1.0 s) = −1.0 i + 4.5 j m/s and a · v = −7.75 m^2/s^3 < 0, so the acceleration has a component opposite the velocity.
steps: a · v = (1.0)(−1.0) + (−1.5)(4.5) = −7.75; a negative value means the speed is decreasing.
Check: speed^2 = (t − 2.0)^2 + (6.0 − 1.5t)^2 = 3.25t^2 − 22t + 40, whose derivative 6.5t − 22 is −15.5 m^2/s^3 at t = 1.0 s, which is negative.

items.prompt:
Paper investigation with supplied, invented data; it does not replace hands-on laboratory work, and it does not count toward the AP Course Audit or college lab credit. A student releases a cart from rest at x = 0 on a long, straight, slightly tilted track. A motion sensor records the cart's position x along the track, with down the track positive.
| t (s) | 0 | 0.40 | 0.80 | 1.20 | 1.60 | 2.00 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| x (m) | 0.000 | 0.052 | 0.196 | 0.445 | 0.792 | 1.230 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Estimate the cart's velocity at t = 1.20 s from the data. Show your method.

rubric.criterion: Uses a symmetric difference with the readings at 0.80 s and 1.60 s (or a tangent drawn on a position–time graph).
Gets about 0.75 m/s (accept 0.73–0.76 m/s).

steps: The nearest readings on either side of 1.20 s are at 0.80 s and 1.60 s.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The student suspects that the acceleration is constant. Choose quantities to graph so that the data fall on a straight line if the suspicion is correct, compute the values you need, and plot them on the grid provided. Draw a best-fit line.

rubric.criterion: Chooses x against t^2, because x = ½at^2 for a start from rest.
Plots the points on labeled, scaled axes and draws a single best-fit straight line.

parts.answer: Graph x against t^2 (t^2 = 0, 0.16, 0.64, 1.44, 2.56, 4.00 s^2); the points lie close to a straight line through the origin.
steps: With a constant and v_0 = 0, x = (a/2)t^2, which is linear in t^2 with slope a/2.
Square each time and plot (t^2, x).

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Use your graph to determine the cart's acceleration.

rubric.criterion: Finds the slope of the best-fit line, about 0.31 m/s^2 (accept 0.29–0.32 m/s^2), from points on the line rather than a single data point.

steps: The line passes near (0, 0) and (4.00 s^2, 1.23 m), so its slope is about 0.31 m/s^2.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Compare your estimate from part (a) with the velocity the constant-acceleration model gives at t = 1.20 s. Explain why the method in part (a) works well for this motion.

rubric.criterion: Computes v = at ≈ 0.62 × 1.20 = 0.74 m/s and states that it agrees with part (a) to within about 1%.
Explains that for a quadratic x(t) the symmetric difference over an interval equals the derivative at the interval's midpoint.

parts.answer: The model gives v = (0.62 m/s^2)(1.20 s) = 0.74 m/s, within about 1% of 0.745 m/s. For x = ½at^2 the slope of the secant from 0.80 s to 1.60 s equals the tangent slope at the midpoint, 1.20 s, so the estimate is exact apart from measurement error.
steps: Secant slope of ½at^2 from t − h to t + h is ½a(4th)/(2h) = at, the exact derivative at t.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: In a second run, the sensor's zero is set 0.050 m behind the cart's starting point, so every position reading is 0.050 m too large. Describe how the graph from part (b) would change and whether the acceleration found from it would change.

rubric.criterion: States that the line shifts up by 0.050 m (an intercept of 0.050 m) while the slope, and so the acceleration, is unchanged.

parts.answer: Every point moves up by 0.050 m, so the best-fit line has a vertical intercept of 0.050 m instead of passing through the origin. The slope, and therefore the acceleration, does not change.
steps: Adding a constant to every x shifts the graph vertically.
The slope depends on changes in x, which the offset does not affect.
